dedupe_keys.name: epfl ethos lab occuembed official official code implementation of the paper occuembed occupancy extraction merged with building energy disaggregation for occupant responsive operation at scale accepted by energy and buildings

description: The EPFL ETHOS Lab authors publish OccuEMBED code for deriving occupancy from building-energy data. Zenodo archives the release under CC BY 4.0 and links a public repository. The README describes differentiable modelling of stochastic occupancy schedules and separate plug-load, lighting and HVAC components, with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network energy-signature component. The model can support occupant-responsive building control or demand simulations when suitable whole-building load data are available. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this implementation. Coverage depends on the measured building and reference schedules supplied by the user; it is not a public global occupancy time series. A limitation is that inferred occupancy can reflect equipment and HVAC assumptions as well as actual presence, so transfer requires local validation. The repository lists PyTorch and related Python dependencies, while the archived release itself was not executed. The paper is described as accepted by Energy and Buildings, but publication details were not independently checked. No occupancy estimate was reproduced.
